headline: PHP's fixes are out and the Foundation explains the leak; a backdoored LiteLLM release hit PyPI; Moscow says it's ready in principle to talk again; SpaceX's rally lifts the DAX to 25,645.

stories.title: PHP's fixes are out, hosts race to patch, and the PHP Foundation explains how the embargo broke
facts: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 shipped at 16:00 Berlin and fix CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619; the Foundation says anyone running PHP must update now.
CVE-2026-109618: hitting memory_limit at the wrong moment corrupts memory; on Apache with mod_php an unauthenticated request got full code execution with default settings.
CVE-2026-109619: a fatal error can leave a worker pointing at the previous request's freed memory; code execution was shown against a real app on mod_php.
The real CVSS score is 9.2, not the leaked 10.0. The release moved up a day after the CVE IDs leaked on Tuesday, and Chainguard published fixed images 6 hours early.
Calif found it using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol under Patch the Planet, with Wiz and OpenAI reporting independently; OpenAI put out a Codex skill that checks PHP versions.
Patching in the wild: Laravel Cloud rolled out region by region, Ubuntu backported the fix quickly, and Cloudflare's CEO says a new WAF rule is on free for all customers.
The Foundation admits the root cause was first spotted in 2024, and the fix stalled for months because of team consensus rules and too few engine experts.
stories.whyItMatters: If you run PHP anywhere, the patch is the only real fix: PoCs were already circulating before the release. The Foundation is asking companies that depend on PHP to fund more security engineers.

image.alt: PHP Foundation share card for the October 21 security release post

stories.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI shipped a credential stealer and a backdoor
facts: All seven wheels of litellm 1.107.0 install three extra files that run in every Python process on the host, even ones that never import litellm.
The stealer grabs SSH keys, cloud and CI secrets, browser passwords, AI-tool tokens (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and more) and the provider keys in a LiteLLM proxy database.
A sitecustomize.py daemon checked an attacker GitHub file hourly for a server and ran whatever code it returned.
The release was on PyPI from about 13:40 to 15:40 Berlin and has been removed; 1.106.2 and the 1.107.0 release candidates are clean.
SafeDep thinks BerriAI's own private release pipeline built it from tampered source; no public commit contains the implant.
stories.whyItMatters: If anything installed 1.107.0, treat that machine's secrets as stolen: look for cook.pth or sitecustomize.py in site-packages and rotate keys.

image.alt: SafeDep banner for the LiteLLM PyPI compromise write-up

stories.title: Kremlin says it's ready "in principle" to restart talks with Kyiv and Washington, maybe around 10 November
facts: Putin aide Yuri Ushakov spoke after about three hours of talks between Putin and Witkoff in St Petersburg.
He floated a new round around 10 November, possibly in Abu Dhabi, focused on a post-war "security system" for Russia and Ukraine.
A US official told the BBC that Kyiv agreed in Oslo, and Moscow on Wednesday, to a technical-level US–Russia–Ukraine meeting.
Ushakov called the ideas from Oslo not very "useful" and repeated that Russian troops were advancing along the whole front.
stories.whyItMatters: It's the first agreement to resume talks since they were paused in February, but Moscow hasn't moved on substance.

image.alt: Putin and Witkoff at their meeting in St Petersburg

stories.title: SpaceX jumps about 11% on merger talk, lifting European markets; Tesla reports tonight
facts: SpaceX rose 11% on Wednesday, Reuters says, adding about $210bn in market value if the gains hold; Tesla was up more than 3%.
Musk says the special committees haven't agreed terms yet, and the Tesla side needs 50% of all shares, not only the ones that vote.
RBC and JPMorgan analysts expect Tesla holders to want a 20–35% premium; others expect none.
The DAX closed up 1.35% at 25,645, led by SAP (+3.5%), with Rheinmetall down 3.2%; Brent was flat at $108.84.
Tesla's Q3 earnings call is tonight at 23:30 Berlin.

stories.title: OpenAI's models come to Google Cloud, and Anthropic's public IPO filing could land Friday
facts: OpenAI and Google Cloud are bringing OpenAI's frontier models and Codex workflows into Google Cloud's Model Garden, sold via Google Cloud Marketplace.
Google Cloud says that makes it the only hyperscaler offering all three leading closed model families.
Yahoo Finance, citing three people, says Anthropic could make its S-1 public as soon as Friday; IFR says Oct 26, with a roadshow from Nov 9.
Wall Street is talking about a raise of up to $100bn at about a $2trn valuation; Anthropic hasn't commented on timing.
Separately, physicist Christopher Stubbs, a former Harvard dean of science, joined Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust.

image.alt: OpenAI announcement card: OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud

stories.title: Berlin wants natural-hazard cover in every new home insurance policy
facts: Justice Minister Hubig and Finance Minister Klingbeil (both SPD) put out key points for a law: new building policies would cover floods, heavy rain and earthquakes by default.
Owners would pay at most €20,000 themselves per claim; a cheaper minimum cover with up to €100,000 excess is also being looked at.
Existing policies would be extended, automatically after a year if owners don't respond to the insurer's offer.
The ministries want to check whether landlords can be banned from passing the cost on to tenants.
The insurers' association GDV says a mandate alone prevents no damage and wants binding prevention plus state reinsurance.
stories.whyItMatters: Spiegel says more than 40% of homes in Germany aren't insured against flooding today. A draft bill was announced for Q1 2027.

facts.text: The US Supreme Court temporarily blocked the Trump administration from denying transgender federal prisoners certain medical treatments.
Toledo, Ohio: officials ordered nearly 1,000 residents to evacuate after a chemical tank explosion caused a hazardous leak.
Times/Siena poll: Trump's approval hit a new low two weeks before the midterms, driven by frustration over the economy.
Private equity firms reportedly explored buying Xbox, valuing Microsoft's gaming arm at $100–150bn.
Merz at the Berlin Global Dialogue: no escalation with China, but unfair trade practices won't go unanswered.
A new alliance, "Gen Z steht auf", is calling for nationwide protests modelled on France's, while distancing itself from violence; Frankfurt is meant to be a hub.
DuckDB 2.0.0 LTS "Cinnamon Teal": Quack remote protocol, async I/O, a VARIANT type, agent mode, triggers and an extensible SQL parser.
Node.js shipped security releases for 26.x, 24.x and 22.x too, including a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write that allows remote code execution.
eMudhra fallout: Deno 2.9.8 distrusts the compromised CAs, Bun merged blocked-key checks plus NSS 3.131.1 roots, and the PSF says update certifi, pip and uv.
GitHub CLI can now use expiring, auto-refreshing OAuth tokens (public preview, opt in with --expiring).
Colin McDonnell's Motherload imports .md, .toml, .yaml, .csv and .env files into TypeScript with full types, built on TS 7.1 content mappers.
